Bill.BriefDescription: Establishing a training program for managers of manufactured housing communities.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to establishing a training program for managers ofmanufactured housing communities; amending RCW 59.30.070; adding a newchapter to Title 59 RCW; prescribing penalties; and providing effectivedates.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The purpose of this chapter is to establisha training program for managers of manufactured housing communities.

The definitions in this section applythroughout this chapter unless the context clearly requires otherwise. (1) "Manufactured housing community" has the same meaning asprovided in RCW 59.20.030. (2) "Manufactured housing community management" means thoseactions, functions, or duties related to the management of amanufactured housing community including, but not limited to, thecollection of rent and other charges, renting mobile home lots, theenforcement of the terms of tenancy, and the implementation of landlordand tenant duties and responsibilities under chapter 59.20 RCW. p. 1 SHB 1590 (3) "Manufactured housing community manager" means a person whoperforms manufactured housing community management, and is required tobe trained under this chapter to perform manufactured housing communitymanagement services. (4) "Training program" means the manufactured housing communitymanager training program established pursuant to this chapter andadministered by the attorney general under the manufactured/mobile homedispute resolution program.

(1) A person must not manage a manufacturedhousing community in this state beyond the grace period identified insubsection (3) of this section until the person has completed thetraining program. (2) An owner of a manufactured housing community is not required tobe trained under this chapter if the owner employs a resident manager,property manager, or independent contract manager who has completed thetraining program to perform manufactured housing community managementduties. (3) If a person becomes a manufactured housing community managerand has not previously completed the training program, the person mustcomplete the training program within one year of beginning employment.

(1) Any person required to be trained as amanufactured housing community manager must acquire a certificate ofcompletion of training from the attorney general. (2) The certificate of completion of training must: (a) Be made available for view by the public; and (b) Indicate that the person has satisfactorily completed a minimumof four hours of training as prescribed under subsection (4) of thissection. (3) A certificate of completion of training is effective upon thedate of issue and is valid for one year. (4) A minimum of four hours of manufactured housing communitymanager training is required annually.

(1) The attorney general under themanufactured/mobile home dispute resolution program must administer thetraining program. SHB 1590 p. 2 (2) The attorney general must develop the curriculum for thetraining program with input from statewide associations representingmanufacturing housing community tenants and owners. (3) The attorney general must issue certificates of completion oftraining to persons who have successfully completed the trainingprogram, and must maintain a list of the names of these persons to bemade available to the public. (4) The attorney general may charge a fee for the training programto recover the costs of the training program, but only to the extentfunds are not available in the manufactured/mobile home disputeresolution program account to cover the costs of the training program. (5) The attorney general may enforce this chapter.

The attorney general is not responsible forthe conduct of a landlord, manager, owner, or other person attending orrequired to attend the training program. This chapter does not createa cause of action against the attorney general related to the trainingprogram or a violation of this chapter by any person required to attendthe training program.
A violation of this chapter is a class 1civil infraction under RCW 7.80.120.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 59.30.070 and 2007 c 431 s 8 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The manufactured/mobile home dispute resolution program account iscreated in the custody of the state treasurer. All receipts fromsources directed to the manufactured/mobile home dispute resolutionprogram must be deposited in the account. Expenditures from theaccount may be used only for the costs associated with administeringthe manufactured/mobile home dispute resolution program, including thetraining program under chapter 59.- RCW (the new chapter created insection 12 of this act). Only the attorney general or the attorneygeneral's designee may authorize expenditures from the account. Theaccount is subject to allotment procedures under chapter 43.88 RCW, butan appropriation is not required for expenditures.

If any provision of this act or itsapplication to any person or circumstance is held invalid, theremainder of the act or the application of the provision to otherpersons or circumstances is not affected.
Sections 3 through 5 of this act takeeffect July 1, 2014.
Except for sections 3 through 5 of thisact, this act takes effect August 1, 2013.
Sections 1 through 7 of this act constitutea new chapter in Title 59 RCW.
